newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 13.

text.p: PRAVO - Petrol prices will increase significantly from Thursday, according to Vaclav Loula, the sales director of Benzina a.s., the largest petrol seller in the country. All types of petrol are scheduled to increase by 1.40 crowns and diesel fuel is to increase by 0.70 crowns.

- The Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs is preparing a new method for aiding the elderly and the physically disabled, according to the Minister, Jindrich Vodicka. These citizens should receive from between 500 and 7,500 crowns monthly, he added.

- Even though only Czechs and Czech companies are allowed to participate in the tender for the privatisation of 89 percent of the shares for Jan Becher-Karlovarska Becherovka, it will still end up in foreign hands, according to Hans Ahlers, the mnager of the marketing firm which represents Germany's Underberg.

- The government will meet today to discuss how to financially support the reconstruction of apartments and houses after the recent floods. Currently the government has agreed to provide families whose housing was completely destroyed with 150,000 crowns in the form of a grant and 850,000 crowns in the form of a mortgage.
- A free trade agreement between Turkey and The Czech Republic will likely be signed in the fall, according to the the Czech trade agency.

- Kovohute Bridlicina posted an increase in gross profit from 13.3 million crowns in the first half of last year to 66.5 million crowns in the first half of this year with turnover increasing by 12 percent to 1.69 billion crowns, according to the company's general manager, Ondrej Hradil.

HOSPODARKSE NOVINY - Foreign individuals and companies whos wish to receive loans or want to issue their stocks on the Czech market may have the chance in the coming year, though 1999 is a more likely date, according to Finance Minister, Ivan Pilip. On the other hand these plans do not allow for foreign nationals to purchase property in the Czech Republic.

- Vagonska Ceska Lipa a.s., has lowered its basic capital from 192.479 million crowns to 19.247 million crowns in order to offset their losses from last year of 111.373 million crowns, according to Jindra Bartosova, an aide to the board of directors.
